edges.label: Requires address isolation
details: Runtimes assume a flat, contiguous memory space.
Delegates physical memory fragmentation and swapping to the OS via Paging.
Requires CPU traps for page faults to dynamically allocate physical RAM.

edges.label: Relies on TLB
details: OS virtual memory manager is software, too slow to translate addresses on every instruction.
Relies entirely on the hardware Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB).
If the MMU doesn't support the page structures, VM is impossible.

edges.label: Assumes reliable stream
details: Distributed consensus algorithms (Raft/Paxos) assume messages arrive.
Relies on TCP for connection-oriented, guaranteed in-order delivery.
TCP hides the underlying packet loss of the raw IP layer.

edges.label: Implemented via B-Trees
details: Relational DBs cannot scan raw disk sectors efficiently.
Rely exclusively on B-Tree and B+Tree data structures for O(log n) lookups.
The tree node size is mathematically calibrated to match the hardware disk block size.

edges.label: Transports via HTTP/TLS
details: Software engineering abstracts remote calls as APIs (REST/GraphQL).
These rely entirely on HTTP for uniform semantics (GET/POST).
Relies on TLS for asymmetric cryptographic handshakes to secure the payload.
